title.narrative: Innovation ecosystem for the circularity of plastics, reduction of consumption, and disposal of single-use plastic in the HORECA sector (Plastic IP)

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project aims to benefit millions of people in Brazil by promoting circularity and fostering an enabling regulatory environment. This will drive innovation and investment in sustainable packaging solutions, creating new market opportunities and jobs in the green economy, including for women. The project targets less developed cities such as Salvador and Belém, fostering regional development and economic growth. Municipal governments in these cities support the project through co-financing, recognizing its potential to boost the local economy. Key socio-economic benefits include: 1. Job Creation and Economic Growth: Promoting circularity will drive innovation, create jobs, and foster regional development, especially in less developed cities like Salvador and Belém. 2. Cost Reduction for Local Businesses: Implementing circular solutions will help local businesses reduce costs associated with plastic waste management and regulatory compliance, enhancing their competitiveness. 3. Enhanced Gender Equality: The project will improve gender equality by providing opportunities for women in the green economy, fostering a more inclusive HORECA sector. 4. Regional Development: By targeting less developed cities and fostering local initiatives, the project will drive regional development and economic growth. 5. Documentation and Reporting: Progress, including cost-benefit analyses and socio-economic impacts, will be documented and shared with stakeholders to ensure transparency and knowledge transfer. Additionally, by Y5 Q4, at least 40% of pilots will demonstrate positive socio-economic effects, such as increased income, job creation, and cost savings for HORECA establishments. This target underscores the project's commitment to delivering tangible socio-economic benefits, contributing to a more sustainable and inclusive economy.

To advance plastic circularity in the Food and Beverage sector working with the HORECA sector (hospitality, restaurant and catering) creating a conducive policy and regulatory environment piloted in coastal cities in Brazil.
